findings.evidence: The only use is Mathlib’s `exteriorPower.finrank_eq` at line 42, whose signature requires `Nontrivial`; the theorem’s conclusion remains valid in the complementary subsingleton case.
findings.fix: Remove `[Nontrivial R]` and split the proof with `subsingleton_or_nontrivial R`, using the existing finrank argument in the nontrivial branch.
findings.issue: `exteriorPower.eq_zero_of_finrank_lt` unnecessarily requires `[Nontrivial R]`; over a subsingleton ring every module, including the exterior power, is already subsingleton.

findings.evidence: Mathlib’s `FDRep.of` at `RepresentationTheory/FDRep.lean:123` assumes `[CommRing R]` and `[Module.Finite R V]`; `ExteriorPower/Basis.lean:27` supplies `Module.Finite R (⋀[R]^n M)` from finiteness of `M`. Nearby `stdFDRep` is likewise declared under `[CommRing k]`.
findings.fix: Move `extPowerFDRep` into the `CommRing` section and give it the signature `[CommRing k] → FDRep k (GL (Fin n) k)`.
findings.issue: `extPowerFDRep` is restricted to fields although `FDRep` and this exterior power are available over any commutative ring.

summary: Two declarations impose stronger scalar assumptions than their constructions require.
